key_concepts: Physical changes such as dissolving or state changes do not form new substances.
Chemical changes produce new substances with different composition.
A chemical change results from a chemical reaction.
Reactants are the atoms and molecules that interact in a chemical reaction.
Products are the atoms and molecules produced by a chemical reaction.
In a chemical reaction, atoms are neither created nor destroyed.
Chemical reactions involve breaking bonds in reactants, rearranging atoms, and forming new
Chemical reactions can be represented by word equations and skeleton equations.
Skeleton equations show the chemical formulas of reactants and products.

Oxygen is necessary for combustion; removing oxygen stops burning.
Rusting of iron and hydrolysis of calcium carbide are examples of chemical changes.
